Dev pauses with the equipment case in hand.

“The hearing-assistance kit,” he says. “The new receivers turned up early, so I was getting them charged, labelled, and talking to the booth equipment. Quiet work, mostly.”

He nods toward the auditorium doors, where Rosa and Martin are now at work among the boards.

“The useful bit needs the room: one person sends test audio, another walks the seats and checks what comes through. Hana was going to help, but I hadn’t checked the diary. That part waits until Nell finds us a slot.”

Nell glances up from the rota sheet. “I will find one.”

“I know,” Dev says. “I’m not trying to turn this into an emergency.” He shifts the case against his leg. “There’s still plenty I can finish upstairs without making a noise.”

From behind the auditorium doors comes the faint scrape of a board being adjusted against the side wall, followed by Rosa’s voice, too muffled to make out.

Dev looks toward the stairs. “Anyway. That’s the glamorous answer. Batteries, settings, and me discovering which cable I’ve put in the wrong pocket.”
